summary: One focused behavior: land the private roster's tier-1 (5-7 tiny ambient/schooling organisms) as data-driven CreatureDef entries on the ST-02 framework, spawned in production world data, each with a headless signature-rule test. The organisms are uniform data entries of one tier batch, so a per-organism split is invalid (children would keep the same 2 criteria and 3 subsystems). Three named changed responsibilities, at the leaf cap: creature simulation (defs + school parameters in hiddenCreatures.ts, including the conditional in-place ST-02 school extension or a <=~120-line bespoke controller per section 19 - still within this one responsibility), world content data (spawns/caps in worldData.ts), headless scenario tests (per-species scenarios via src/sim/scenario.ts). Renderer is explicitly not changed (WI-02b reuse, data-parameterized silhouettes). Criteria AC-roster-count and AC-roster-tests are carried from ST-03 verbatim, matching the story's assignment to all four children; the roster-wide count check, test audit, and spoiler audit are explicitly owned by dependent WI-03d, so cross-child proof has a named owner. depends_on: [] is correct: ST-01/ST-02 are inherited through the story, and the story confirms WI-03a is independent of its siblings. Evidence is tier-scoped (per-species scenarios, tier world-data check as a portion of the roster-wide check, one presentation spot-check) with no whole-game verification or open-ended defect fixing. Handoff names concrete files, request sections, WI-01b for organism ids, design_private/ as source of truth, spoiler-safe commit style, and an explicit falsifiable assumption about school-behavior reuse; a fresh implementer can proceed without reconstructing the project.
